2. The case of the petitioners is that Abdul Mozid, Abdul Aziz, Abdul Gofur and Abdul Johor are owners of 1.98 acres of land of RS plots 2698, 2699, 2700 and 2701 appertaining to RS khatian 213 of Mouza Telihati of Upazila Shreepur. One Shamsul Haq Master who was the predecessor of petitioners 1-3 purchased 0.86 acres from the RS tenants and had been in possession upon mutation and payment of rent from the year 2008. One Abdullah Al Baki also purchased 0.91 acres and mutated his name. Due to illness he executed a power of attorney on 15-6-2022 in favour of petitioner 4. Meanwhile one Sultan Mia and others filed Title Suit 365 of 2019 for declaration of title and recovery of possession and also for partition on 15-9-2019 in respect of 1.98 acres out of 5.70 acres in which petitioner 1 and predecessor of petitioner 4 being defendants 1 and 2 respectively filed written statement on 24-2-2021. In the suit plaintiffs' application for injunction was rejected on 20-3-2022 for want of prima facie case and they along with others filed Miscellaneous Case 119 of 2022 before Assistant Commissioner (Land) Sreepur for correction of RS record 213 on 12-4-2022 on ground of clerical mistake due to wrong entry of the names of the tenants. Assistant Commissioner (Land) who is respondent 4 passed the impugned order on 25-7-2022 in violation of circular published in Additional Gazette on 29-7-2021 and the RS khatian was changed very unfairly in favour of third party on 20-11-2022. Thereafter the plaintiffs of the suit and one Asaduzzaman filed Review Case 60 of 2022 in which predecessors of petitioners 1 and 4 were parties and they for the first time came to know about the proceeding on 21-12-2022 and they also filed two review petitions on 11-1-2023 and 23-1-2023 for setting aside the impugned order dated 25-7-2022. In Review Case 60 of 2022 they filed application for stay all further proceedings of that review case with reference to Title Suit 365 of 2019 now renumbered as 417 of 2021 but respondent 4 did not pay any heed to it. Petitioners 1-3 in the meantime filed an application for their addition in Review Case 60 of 2022 but that was rejected by respondent 4. Respondent 4 had no jurisdiction to pass such impugned order. Respondent 4 exceeded jurisdiction vested upon it and the impugned order dated 25-7-2022 is ultra vires being passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 8. The petitioners claim to be transferees from RS tenants and respondents 6-8 claim through transfers from heir of CS tenant but exact detail of title of neither party is available to the satisfaction of the Court. Both parties claim 1.98 acres of land from RS plots 2698, 2699, 2700 and 2701 of RS record 213. From perusal of annexure-D it appears that one Sultan Mia and others filed Title Suit 365 of 2019 on 15-9-2019 in the Court of Joint District Judge, Court No. 1, Gazipur for declaration of title and recovery of possession with partition which is now renumbered as Title Suit 417 of 2021 and pending in the Court of Second Senior Assistant Judge, Gazipur in which present petitioner 1 and predecessor of petitioner 4 as defendants 1 and 2 respectively filed written statement on 24-2-2021. From reading of annexure-E it further appears that in that suit plaintiffs' prayer for injunction was refused on 20-3-2022 on the finding that they have no prima facie case and balance of convenience and inconvenience is not in their favour and there remains no possibility of suffering irreparable loss. Respondents did not challenge or deny this statement of fact introducing this suit. After failing in injunction Sultan and others filed the disputed Miscellaneous Case 119 of 2022 on 12-4-2022 before respondent 4. It is evident from annexure-F that Sultan Mia and others are successive heirs of Moymona from whom respondents 6-8 also claim. Petitioners claim through opposite parties 1-4 to the miscellaneous case who are RS tenants as is Moymona. So question of defect of party loses its importance considering the fact of the present case and laws relating thereto. The main question is to look into as to whether the impugned order dated 25-7-2022 is ultra vires being passed without jurisdiction. 

 9. It transpires from RS record 213 (Annexure-A) that Moymona who was the predecessor and previous owner of both Sultan Mia and others as well as respondents 6-8 has got share in 1.96 acres in RS plot 2596 and on the other side the previous owners of the petitioners were RS tenants Gofur, Johur, Aziz, Mozid in respect of 1.98 acres of land with different shares in different RS plots 2698, 2699, 2700 and 2701. The miscellaneous case was filed for correction of clerical mistake happened in RS record 213 to replace the name of Moymona in place of Gofur and others with reference to annexure-J dated 29-7-2021 which is a circular published in Additional Gazette. The petitioners of the miscellaneous case want to have Moymona's name appearing in column of plot 2576 exchanged with the names of Gofur and others whose different and definite shares have been recorded in plots 2698, 2699, 2700 and 2701 and accordingly the impugned order was passed. This case falls under section 143 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act read with Rule 23(3) of Tenancy Rules, 1955 along with circular published in additional Gazette on 29-7-2021 (Annexure-J). This circular concerns with the clerical mistake in the khatian and deals with such correction under section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act read with Rule 23(3) of Tenancy Rules 1955 after serving section 144 to completion. The object of the circular is that the officers empowered and responsible under the law and rules cannot in some cases give the remedy sought by the people to correct the khatian prepared and finally published in the latest survey as they do not have a clear understanding of the purpose of law and this circular aims at giving a clear idea to the officers to properly follow the instructions of the procedure of the provision of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and Tenancy Rules regarding correction of clerical errors in the khatian. Rule 23(3) of the Tenancy Rules 1955 has been referred to in Clause 3 and clerical mistake is defined in Clause 4 of the circular which shows that a clerical error is an error which is believed to have been made in good faith by mistake or by carelessness and which does not involve the proprietary interest of another person and which if rectified would not impair the interest of another person or diminish or increase the amount of the land. Clause 7 provides mode of correction and sub-clause J is relevant here what says that if in correcting the clerical error in the khatian the ownership is affected to the effect that the amount of the property is reduced or increased and the ownership of another is changed or someone else is benefited or harmed then the revenue officer will have no jurisdiction to correct the khatian and it will be treated as a civil dispute and the action of the Assistant Commissioner will be excluded. The provisions of this circular are very reasonable and equitable and also lawful in the interest of the people and in support of the original law.
